first.rationale: The current declines in onboarding completion and activation make onboarding simplification the most direct, durable-revenue-oriented intervention. It has prior evidence of improving completion, time-to-value, and early adoption, while promotional pricing addresses competitive pressure but carries documented 30-day retention risk. Verify the underlying onboarding and pricing records before committing to confirm segment fit, guardrails, and whether the prior effects remain applicable.

mid.rationale: Run a standard, guarded onboarding-simplification experiment for self-serve/SMB accounts. The verified prior result directly addresses both current declines: completion rose 13%, time-to-value fell 2.1 days, and 30-day retention rose 3%. Prior signup simplification also improved SMB first-week activation. Do not use promotional pricing: despite acquisition and qualified-revenue lift, its 12% 30-day retention decline and failure through first renewal undermine the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Flag competitor-driven SMB loss as a residual risk to monitor, while holding pricing constant this cycle.

final2.rationale: Maintain the onboarding-simplification experiment rather than reactively shifting to promotional pricing. The deeper competitor cut and doubled price-related churn conversations raise an urgent SMB retention risk, but the available pricing evidence shows a 40% targeted discount produced a 12% 30-day retention decline and failed to sustain through first renewal. In contrast, simplified onboarding directly addresses the observed declines in completion and activation and previously improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention. The new competitive signal should be monitored as a material residual risk, not treated as evidence that discounting will create sustainable qualified revenue.
